# Flizy

> Send crypto from WhatsApp or Telegram, only to destinations approved in advance. GIWA-first, testnet.

Money commands run in the chat app the user already has, and the same account can be linked
on WhatsApp and Telegram at once. Transfers only reach destinations the user approved on the
site, so a stolen phone cannot add a new payout address. Swaps only go through allowlisted
DEX routers, with fees disclosed before confirmation. Currently running on GIWA Sepolia
testnet with source-verified contracts.

## Site

- / : Product home and four-step overview
- /how-it-works : Full user guide and commands for both chat apps
- /docs : Why trusted addresses exist (security)
- /signup : Create account
- /login : Sign in
- /dashboard : Wallet, PIN, trusted people, link code for WhatsApp or Telegram
- /dashboard/swap : Swap FLZ and ETH, add or remove liquidity
- /claim/:token : Claim funds reserved for a phone number

## Channels

- WhatsApp: commands are prefixed, for example `flizy send 0.01 to john`, then `confirm`.
- Telegram: slash commands, for example `/send 0.01 to john`, confirm by button or by typing.
- One site link code binds either channel. Identity is proven by that code, because only a
  logged-in account holder can generate one.
- Claims are addressed to a phone number, so they can be redeemed from either channel by
  whoever owns that number. One phone belongs to exactly one account.
- Sending to a phone number always reserves the funds, whether or not that number is
  already on Flizy. If it is, the owner is notified in their chat app immediately and
  claims it there. Money never arrives in a wallet unannounced, and a number that is not
  on Flizy is never messaged out of the blue. The sender can cancel until it is claimed.

## When to read

- Read /how-it-works to onboard a human user on WhatsApp or Telegram.
- Read /docs when a send is rejected for destination policy.
- Read /dashboard flows for link codes and trusted address management.
